name: Academy 64 Interactive Missions Math & Logic Truth
note: This gate has now been wrong in two different ways, and both were the same mistake wearing different clothes. First it held a stale expected count of 27/54, so deleting a stage made the numbers agree and it printed PERFECT — it rewarded the deletion it existed to prevent. Then it turned out to check the guide text for the answer and never the title, and 34 of 64 missions had been naming the wrong number in their titles across all thirteen languages. In both cases the gate looked at whether something was present rather than whether two things agreed. The counts are pinned to constants now, and every number a title or guide claims is checked twice: against the target cell the screen actually draws, and against what the other twelve languages say about the same puzzle. Neither check alone is enough — the first passes a title that swaps the answer for the eliminated candidate, the second passes a mistake all thirteen languages share — and the mutation list below records the SURVIVED verdict that proved it.

mutations.name: a whole practice stage is dropped from the aggregator
mutations.why: This gate once held a stale expected count of 27/54. Removing a stage made the two numbers agree and it printed PERFECT — it rewarded the very deletion it existed to prevent. The counts are pinned to constants now, and this is the mutation that proves it.

mutations.name: a title names a number the puzzle never produces
mutations.why: This is the shipped bug, restored. The title said [9] 확정 while correctVal was 6 — in all thirteen languages, because the Korean source was wrong and twelve translations carried it faithfully. It survived for months behind a gate that read the guide and never the title, so this mutation is the only reason to believe the new half of the check works. Note the digit chosen: 9 is not the answer and not the eliminated candidate, so no legitimate reading of the puzzle allows it.

mutations.name: one language's guide swaps the answer for the candidate the technique removes
mutations.why: The hole in the first check, and the reason a second one exists. The allowed set holds two values — the answer and the eliminated candidate — because titles legitimately name either ('eliminate [8] from the box' is true when 8 is what gets removed). So swapping one for the other stays inside the allowed set and the first check passes it; this mutation was recorded SURVIVED before the cross-language comparison was added. What catches it is that thirteen languages describe one puzzle: ko now says [7] while ja and both Chinese locales still say [4], and that disagreement is detectable without parsing any grammar. (2026-09-18: X-Wing 예제가 자체 생성 퍼즐로 바뀌며 제목에 숫자가 없어져, 같은 구멍을 안내문에서 연다 — 한국어만 지워지는 후보 5를 답이라고 말하게 한다.)
mutations.expectFailure: names different numbers in different languages

mutations.name: the eliminated candidate is deleted from the target cell
mutations.why: The allowed set is derived from cells[targetIndex].eliminatedNotes, so that field is load-bearing for the check and not merely decoration for the diagram. Removing it narrows the allowed set to correctVal alone, which must then reject the titles that legitimately name the eliminated value. If this mutation survives, the derivation is not actually reading the cell and the check has quietly become a copy again.

mutations.name: a hidden-subset practice asks for a digit the technique does not decide
mutations.why: The shipped defect, restored. Six hidden pair/triple/quad practices put the target on a cell the subset only cleans, not decides — two to four digits still fitted, and the screen answered "correct" because the input matched a stored value. Putting 8 back into the target cell makes it undecided again.

mutations.name: a practice board that no arrangement can satisfy
mutations.why: One shipped board was worse than undecided: the candidates in that box admitted no valid arrangement at all, so the "answer" belonged to a grid that cannot exist. Dropping 2 from a cell that needs it recreates that state. 판이 스스로 완결됐다고 말할 때만(칸 수만큼 숫자가 보일 때) 세므로, 숫자 수는 그대로 두고 세 칸이 같은 두 후보를 나눠 갖게 만든다.

mutations.name: a generated board is stored with one wrong value
mutations.why: The 9x9 examples are in-house puzzles stored cell by cell. One mistyped value leaves a board that still looks plausible but no longer has the solution the answer was checked against.

mutations.name: a generated example asks for a digit that is not the solution
mutations.why: The shipped class of defect: a stored answer the board does not produce. Here the answer is set to the candidate the Swordfish removes, which the old academy did in several places.

mutations.name: a which-candidate-goes question prints its own answer
mutations.why: Missions that ask which candidate is removed are only a question while the guide does not name it.
mutations.find: 목표 칸 r3c3에서 지워지는 후보는 무엇일까요?
mutations.replace: 목표 칸 r3c3에서 지워지는 후보는 무엇일까요? 정답은 [9]입니다.

mutations.name: a 9x9 example strikes out the true digit
mutations.why: Striking the real answer from the target is exactly what several of the old examples did. The gate re-solves the board and refuses any struck candidate that is the true digit.

mutations.name: a cross-hatching picture whose answer is already in the box
mutations.why: Cross-hatching is a hidden single inside one box. If the digit the mission asks for is already placed in that box, the picture teaches nothing and the answer is impossible.

mutations.name: a strategy's theory diagram falls outside every check
mutations.why: BACKLOG A-1 (2026-09-19): the hand-drawn theory diagrams were never checked and 17 of 32 were wrong by the rules.

mutations.name: the theory board strikes a candidate the cell never had
mutations.why: The theory tab's second frame is drawn from eliminations; a wrong entry would teach a deletion that is not there.
